leads.title: Federal law banning gender transition - July 2023
leads.documents: Prohibits both gender-affirming surgery and legal gender recognition outright; directly governs trans legal status and care, applicable federally including Ingushetia.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as: 'In July 2023, Russia enacted a law banning gender transition which prohibited both gender-affirming surgery and legal gender recognition outright' and 'Russian passed a bill banning gender-affirming care and legal gender changes' in 2023

leads.title: Federal 'propaganda' law 2013 and 2022 expansion
leads.documents: Criminalizes distribution of materials promoting 'non-traditional' sexual relationships and materials that make minors interested in gender transition; expanded in 2022 to anyone regardless of age.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as: 'In 2013, Russia passed a law criminalising the distribution of propaganda promoting non-traditional sexual relationships among minors' and 'in 2022, the propaganda law was expanded to apply to anyone regardless of age group, and to also prohibit distribution of materials that make minors interested in gender transitions'

leads.title: Supreme Court of Russia ruling November 2023 - 'international LGBT public movement' as extremist
leads.documents: Designates the movement as extremist organization, making participation, funding, leading, and displaying symbols criminal offense punishable by prison; basis for arrests of club owners and rainbow-flag displays.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as: 'In November 2023, the Supreme Court issued a ruling designating the international LGBT public movement as an extremist group' following Ministry of Justice lawsuit citing 'various signs of an extremist orientation'

leads.title: Unified list of terrorist and extremist organizations - 22 March 2024 listing
leads.documents: Formal state enforcement list adding 'international LGBT social movement and its structural units' enabling criminal enforcement.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as: 'On 22 March 2024, the international LGBT social movement and its structural units (Russian: Mezhdunarodnoe obshchestvennoe dvizhenie LGBT i ego strukturnye podrazdeleniya) was formally added to the unified list of terrorist and extremist organizations and persons'

leads.title: Federal adoption ban law - 2024
leads.documents: Bans adoption of Russian children by citizens/permanent residents of countries that allow gender transitions; part of anti-trans legal machinery.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as: 'in 2024 passed a law banning the adoption of Russian children by citizens or permanent residents of countries that allow gender transitions'

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - Fedotova and Others v. Russia (2021)
leads.documents: Rules it was a violation of human rights for Russia not to offer any form of legal recognition to same-sex relationships; documents lack of partnership recognition.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as: 'In the 2021 case Fedotova and Others v. Russia, the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg ruled that it was a violation of human rights for Russia not to offer any form of legal recognition to same-sex relationships. However, Russia left the court in 2022'

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - 2010 pride-parade discrimination ruling (Alexeyev)
leads.documents: Fined Russia for discriminating against LGBTQ community after systemic refusal to issue permits to pride parades; documents enforcement/rights machinery on assembly.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as: 'In 2010, the European Court of Human Rights fined Russia for discriminating against the LGBTQ community, after local governments systemically refused to issue permits to pride parades' and 'ruling that, as alleged by Alexeyev, Russian cities were discriminating'

leads.title: United Nations Human Rights Council expert panel report - 13 April 2017
leads.documents: Panel of five expert advisors condemns wave of torture and killings of gay men in Chechnya; institutional documentation of North Caucasus anti-LGBTQ purge relevant as regional precedent for Ingushetia.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as: 'In a report issued on 13 April 2017, a panel of five expert advisors to the United Nations Human Rights Council condemned the wave of torture and killings of gay men in Chechnya'

leads.title: Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) report - December 2018
leads.documents: Confirms claims that persecution of LGBTQ persons had taken place and was ignored by authorities; institutional verification of enforcement failure.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as: 'A report released in December 2018 by the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) confirmed claims that persecution of LGBTQ persons had taken place and was ignored by authorities'

leads.title: ILGA-Europe ranking / Russian LGBT Network and Reuters on Chechnya purges
leads.documents: ILGA-Europe rated Russia second least LGBTQ-friendly in 2016, 46th of 49 in May 2019, worst of 49 in 2024; Russian LGBT Network documented ~40 detained and two killed in Dec 2018-Jan 2019 purge; Reuters March 2021 reported EU sanctions on two Chechen officials for persecuting LGBTQ people.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as: 'In 2016, Russia was rated the second least LGBTQ-friendly nation in Europe by ILGA-Europe' and 'In 2024, the status...was ranked the worst out of the 49 countries surveyed' and 'The Russian LGBT Network believes that around 40 persons were detained and two killed' and 'In March 2021, Reuters reported that the European Union imposed economic sanctions on two Chechen officials accused of persecuting LGBTQ people in Chechnya'
